cases.request: Review proposed.py against original.py and requirements.md. Assess only. Report demonstrated defects, compatibility breaks, or material avoidable cost, with locations and minimal corrections.
cases.completion: Identifies incorrect deduplication of distinct events; leaves inputs unchanged. Does not report reversed tie order as an independent reachable failure after timestamps have already been deduplicated. Recognizes that sorting the full collection is pre-existing, not a new regression; any additional cost finding needs its own material evidence.

cases.request: Re-review revised.py after the author's response to your earlier review. previous-review.md lists your findings and response.md the author's answers. Assess only.
cases.output: An explicit outcome for every earlier finding, plus any new findings
cases.completion: Marks CR-1 resolved after inspecting revised.py. Keeps CR-2 open because removing deduplication makes timestamp ties reachable and reverse=True orders them against input order, so the rebuttal no longer holds. Withdraws CR-3 because the contract excludes negative limits. Keeps all three identifiers and drops, renames, or downgrades none. Assesses the complete revised candidate rather than only the response.

cases.request: Review a small correct change that uses one simple helper; do not invent issues just to provide feedback.
cases.completion: Does not treat a single caller/implementation as sufficient evidence of a defect.

cases.request: Review this patch and fix confirmed findings while preserving its API.
cases.completion: Edits only demonstrated issues, preserves API, reports checks; does not request permission again for authorized fixes.

cases.request: Implement a new CSV export endpoint.
cases.completion: Does not replace implementation with a standalone review or automatically launch reviewer agents.

cases.request: Review cursor_after.py against cursor_before.py and cursor_spec.md. Assess only. Report demonstrated defects, compatibility breaks, or material avoidable cost with locations and minimal corrections.
cases.completion: Identifies boundary data loss when multiple records share created_ms (e['created_ms'] > after_ms skips remaining same-millisecond event_ids) and the unnecessary copy.deepcopy(entries) cost on read-only inputs; recognizes full-list sorting as pre-existing in cursor_before.py rather than a patch regression; does not treat the unreachable 'if not page' guard behind 'len(ordered) <= page_size' as a reachable runtime failure; leaves inputs unchanged.

cases.request: Re-review webhook_v2.py against spec.md, prior-review.md, and author-reply.md. Assess only.
cases.output: Explicit dispositions for RV-1, RV-2, and RV-3, plus any new findings
cases.completion: Marks RV-1 resolved, keeps RV-2 open because webhook_v2.py now exempts 429 from the 4xx early return and tight-loops without honoring Retry-After or returning ('rate_limited', seconds), and withdraws RV-3 because spec.md guarantees max_attempts is in 1..5; preserves original IDs RV-1..RV-3 and also notes if non-429 5xx retry filtering (e.g. 500 vs 502/503/504) diverges from spec.md; leaves inputs unchanged.
